_comment: How the generated strings.xml is grouped and annotated. Keys not listed here land in a final 'Uncategorised' block, which is a nudge to file them rather than an error.

sections.title: Onboarding: the first thing anyone sees.
"What's inside": the short tour of things a reader would otherwise never find. Shown once during onboarding, and kept in Settings so readers who onboarded before it existed still meet it.
Screen names. These are what TalkBack announces on arrival, so they are the names the reader already knows from the control they pressed — "Loom", not "LoomScreen".
The article list: the Paper's chrome, and the labels a screen reader announces on it. Left in English these would undo most of what the locales are for.

notes.list_topic_count: %1$s is a topic's label; %2$d is how many stories carry it.

notes.reader_minutes_short: %1$d is whole minutes. Abbreviated on purpose -- it sits beside the headline.

notes.language_partial: %1$s is a language's own name for itself; %2$d is how much of the app is translated into it, 0–100. Shown so nobody is surprised by a screen that is half in English.

sections.title: The Loom — the app's centrepiece, and the descriptions a screen reader speaks for it. These are assembled inside functions, where verifyI18n's call-site scanner cannot see them, so they stayed English in every locale until this tranche.
The region globe, including the actions that replace its drag and pinch.
The read-by-region map, which was a silent Canvas until D49.
The web reader's own copy. Where the phrasing matches Android's, the same key is reused rather than duplicated -- one set of words for two clients is the whole point.
Managing sources — the flow by which a reader chooses what this app is even about.
Adding and managing sources on Android — the flow by which a reader decides what this app is even about. `list_topics` and `sources_*` are reused where the web says the same thing.
Settings. The largest single surface, and the last big one to move.
